exposure: Facemask placement for respiratory support at birth
cohort: The study participants were infants born at 32+0 weeks of gestation or later at two perinatal centres in Melbourne, Australia.
finding: Facemask respiratory support at birth is temporally associated with a decrease in heart rate in a subset of late-preterm and term infants, with 15% experiencing a >10 bpm decrease within 15 seconds.
mod_finding: Mode of birth was found not to be a risk factor for a decrease in heart rate by >10 bpm after facemask placement.
cross-section timing: Up to 120 seconds after facemask placement at birth
